pass_b_english: The people of Israel have a unique relationship with God, which has been clearly stated, so that it may be evident that God is involved in everything.
It was necessary for those who honored ungodliness toward God to be excluded from his care and love.

However, those who were held captive by sin due to ignorance and had fallen under the devil's control were to be killed by the creator of all, and yet they were called to know him and to experience the light of truth.

This is also evident in the words of the all-wise Moses, who said that the people provoked God to jealousy with idols and angered him with their pursuits, as he stated: 'They provoked me to jealousy with those who are not gods, they angered me with their idols; and I will provoke them to jealousy with a nation that is not a nation; with a foolish nation I will anger them' (Deuteronomy 32:21).

The prophetic Melitos also stated that the people provoked God with their idols and pursuits, and as a result, God saw their actions, despised them, and greatly humbled Israel, for it is written: 'They provoked him with their idols and with their pursuits, and the Lord God saw and despised and greatly humbled Israel'.

Nevertheless, if we are to interpret these words spiritually, we must be cautious not to fall into the devil's trap in our minds and hearts, and not to be swayed by the evil idols in our fantasies that call us to licentiousness and perverse pleasures, lest we become prey to Satan and demons.

It is essential to pay attention to the words of Scripture, for they offer a remedy for great sins, as it is written: 'If the spirit of the one in authority rises up against you, do not leave your place, because a remedy will calm great sins' (Proverbs 24:19).
Who among you pays attention to these things? Listen to what is coming.

The divinely inspired writer encourages us to listen carefully, so that we may receive the word with a clear mind and store it in our heart, as the psalmist says: 'I have hidden your word in my heart, that I might not sin against you' (Psalm 119:11).
This is also evident in the 48th psalm, where it is written: 'Hear this, all nations; give ear, all inhabitants of the world' (Psalm 48:1).

Hearing is common to all who have once perceived a sound or some other noise, but paying attention is to bring something of the established things into one's mind, and to store it in both mind and heart.

The prophetic word seeks those who have listened more gently and thoughtfully, so that they may speak about the safety of future things based on past events, as Paul says: 'These things happened to them as examples, and they were written for our instruction, upon whom the ends of the ages have come' (1 Corinthians 10:11).

We must not encounter the stories about him in vain, but rather receive them for the benefit of our soul, and avoid being caught in the same sins, so that we may not fall into the same disasters as they did.
